methods.label: Subtract the circle areas
methods.explanation:
The smaller circular region is contained in the larger one, so the area outside the smaller circle and inside the larger is \(\pi R^2-\pi r^2\). The circles need not have the same center.

The given finite multiplier requires \(b\ne0\) and \(0<r<R\). Since the larger area exceeds the remaining area, \(a/b>1\), so also \(a\ne0\) and \(a-b\ne0\). The area equation is
\[
\pi R^2=\frac ab(\pi R^2-\pi r^2).
\]
Canceling \(\pi\), multiplying by \(b\), and collecting terms gives
\[
(a-b)R^2=ar^2.
\]
Because both radii are positive, taking the positive square root yields
\[
\frac Rr=\sqrt{\frac{a}{a-b}}.
\]
To split this into the separate real square roots used in choice B, assume the customary positive representation \(a>b>0\). Then
\[
R:r=\sqrt a:\sqrt{a-b}.
\]
The positivity convention matters. For example, \(R=2\), \(r=1\), \(a=-4\), and \(b=-3\) give the required area multiplier \(4/3\), but \(\sqrt a\) and \(\sqrt{a-b}\) are not real. Thus the unrestricted wording needs a qualification. Under the recorded ordinary grading convention \(a>b>0\), the answer is \(\boxed{\sqrt a:\sqrt{a-b}}\), choice \(\mathrm B\).
